hook: SCP-3848 is a phenomenon that makes everyone inside one town or county forget a single concept, all at once and for good. Most of the article is a run of case files, each built around a different thing a whole community suddenly can't remember. They start out almost funny, so watch how the tone shifts by the end of the list.
whyItMatters: The containment procedures are mostly about the document itself: copies kept at every site, open to all staff regardless of clearance, memorized by trained specialists, and rewritten under a new item number if the concept of 3848 is ever forgotten. That turns the page you are reading into part of the containment effort. The footnotes also tie it to the idea of the anti-meme, and its tags mark it as an apocalyptic, end-of-the-world scenario.
thingsToNotice:
The dog interview is the centerpiece. The agent has already been briefed three times, finds the word itself unreal, compares looking at photos of his own borzoi to trying to grasp a four-dimensional cube, and in his last line is surprised all over again to learn he owns a dog.

The case list then escalates in stakes rather than strangeness: line fishing in Wilmington, boats in Felixstowe, turn signals in Queens, then how alternating current works, which leaves Mainz without power for three days. The final entry erases the knowledge that murder is illegal and wrong in an Ontario town, where a resident kills his neighbor with a sharpened stone, a Mountie later kills a civilian in front of witnesses, and the results are expunged.

Small details widen the frame. Footnote 1 predicts a full Lethe Scenario by 2035 at the latest, the description suggests a worldwide one may already have happened unnoticed, footnote 5 reveals the Foundation's own three-arrow logo is a low-level memetic reminder symbol, and an edit note is dated 03/03/27.
